concepts.name: Supreme Court: strength, appointment, qualifications, oath, tenure and the Judges Cases
concepts.description: Strength of the Court, appointment of the CJI and other judges, Article 124 qualifications, oath, tenure, and the First, Second and Third Judges Cases with the collegium.
concepts.idea: The Supreme Court is staffed through consultation, and the meaning of consultation was reshaped by three judicial rulings into the collegium.
concepts.rule: Article 124(1) leaves the number of judges to Parliament; the Court began with eight judges and, according to Laxmikanth, has 34 now. Judges are appointed by warrant of the President after consultation with judges (the CJI compulsorily); the senior-most judge becomes CJI by convention. A judge must be a citizen and a High Court judge for five years, a High Court advocate for ten years, or a distinguished jurist; there is no minimum age, retirement is at 65 and the oath is taken before the President. S.P. Gupta (1981) held consultation is not concurrence; the Second Judges Case (1993) reversed it; the 1998 Presidential Reference fixed a collegium of the CJI and four senior-most judges.
concepts.example: A scholar with no court experience can be appointed as distinguished jurist, but the CJI cannot forward a name if two collegium judges object.

questions.q: Dr. Meera, aged 44, is a respected academic in constitutional law. She has never been a judge or an advocate. Which one of the following statements about her eligibility for appointment as a Judge of the Supreme Court is correct?
questions.a: She can be appointed if the President regards her as a distinguished jurist, because no minimum age is prescribed
o: She can be appointed if the President regards her as a distinguished jurist, because no minimum age is prescribed
She is ineligible because every Supreme Court judge must have practised as an advocate of a High Court for at least ten years, and she has not
She is ineligible because the Constitution requires a minimum age of 45 years for a Supreme Court judge, which she has not yet reached
She can be appointed if the Chief Justice of India, and not the President, certifies her as a distinguished jurist
questions.e: Article 124(3) requires citizenship and one of three qualifications: five years as a High Court judge, ten years as a High Court advocate, or being a distinguished jurist in the opinion of the President. No minimum age is fixed; judges retire at 65. Also Laxmikanth ch26 p.415.
w: Ten years at the Bar is only one of three alternative routes; the distinguished-jurist route needs no court experience.
The Constitution prescribes no minimum age for a Supreme Court judge.
The distinguished-jurist test is the opinion of the President, not a certificate of the CJI.

questions.q: The oath or affirmation of a Judge of the Supreme Court differs from that of a High Court judge in which one of the following respects?
questions.a: Before the President or his nominee for a Supreme Court judge, and before the Governor or his nominee for a High Court judge
o: Before the President or his nominee for a Supreme Court judge, and before the Governor or his nominee for a High Court judge
The Supreme Court judge swears to uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India, a pledge that is absent from the oath of a High Court judge
The Supreme Court judge's oath is set out in the Second Schedule, whereas the High Court judge's oath is set out in the Third Schedule
The Supreme Court judge makes it before the Chief Justice of India, whereas the High Court judge makes it before the Chief Justice of the High Court
questions.e: Article 124(6) with the Third Schedule requires a Supreme Court judge to make the oath before the President or a person appointed for the purpose; Article 219 requires a High Court judge to do so before the Governor or his nominee. The content (true faith and allegiance, sovereignty and integrity, duties without fear or favour, affection or ill-will, uphold the Constitution and laws) is the same. Also Laxmikanth ch26 p.415 and ch34 p.509.
w: Both oaths contain the pledge to uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India.
Both oaths are prescribed in the Third Schedule (Articles 124(6) and 219).
Neither oath is administered by a Chief Justice; the authorities are the President and the Governor respectively.

questions.q: In 1998 the President sought the Supreme Court's opinion under Article 143 on the meaning of 'consultation' in Articles 124, 217 and 222. Which one of the following was the result of that opinion?
questions.a: The sole opinion of the CJI was held insufficient; he must consult a collegium of the four senior-most Supreme Court judges
o: The sole opinion of the CJI was held insufficient; he must consult a collegium of the four senior-most Supreme Court judges
'Consultation' was held to mean a mere exchange of views, leaving the President free to disregard the opinion of the Chief Justice of India
The Chief Justice of India was required to consult only his two senior-most colleagues before advising the President, as laid down in 1993
The power to recommend judges was transferred to a commission that included the Union Law Minister and two eminent persons
questions.e: The Third Judges Case (1998) arose from a Presidential Reference. The Court held that the CJI cannot act alone, consultation must involve a plurality of judges, and the collegium is the CJI plus the four senior-most Supreme Court judges. Also Laxmikanth ch26 p.414.
w: That was the First Judges Case (1981), which this opinion did not repeat.
Two senior-most colleagues was the 1993 Second Judges Case formula, widened in 1998.
That describes the NJAC of 2014, which was struck down in 2015; it is not the 1998 opinion.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the appointment of the Chief Justice of India is correct?
questions.a: The President appoints him after consulting such judges as he deems necessary, and the senior-most judge is chosen by convention
o: The President appoints him after consulting such judges as he deems necessary, and the senior-most judge is chosen by convention
Article 124 expressly lays down that the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court shall be appointed as Chief Justice of India, leaving the President no choice
The convention of appointing the senior-most judge has been followed without a break since 1950, even during the Emergency years
The President appoints him after consulting the Governors and the Chief Ministers of the States concerned
questions.e: Per Article 124(2) the CJI is appointed by the President after consulting such SC and High Court judges as he deems necessary; the senior-most judge is chosen by established convention. Laxmikanth ch26 p.415 records the supersessions of 1973 and 1977 and the 1993 ruling that the senior-most judge alone should be appointed.
w: The constitutional text does not mention seniority; it rests on convention and later judicial rulings.
It was departed from in 1973 (A.N. Ray superseded three judges) and in 1977 (M.U. Beg).
Governors are consulted for High Court appointments, not for the Chief Justice of India.

questions.q: Article 124(2A) of the Constitution provides that any question about the age of a Judge of the Supreme Court is to be determined by
questions.a: such authority and in such manner as Parliament may by law provide
o: such authority and in such manner as Parliament may by law provide
the President after consultation with the Chief Justice of India, whose decision is final
the Chief Justice of India, whose decision on the matter is final
a Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court on a reference made by the President
questions.e: Clause (2A) leaves the authority and manner of determining a Supreme Court judge's age to Parliament, giving clarity and uniformity. For a High Court judge the age question is decided by the President after consulting the CJI (Laxmikanth ch34 p.510).
w: This is the rule for a High Court judge, not a Supreme Court judge.
The Constitution gives no such personal power to the Chief Justice of India.
No such reference procedure is provided in Article 124(2A).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the composition of the Supreme Court:

1. Article 124(1) provides for a Chief Justice of India and such number of other judges as Parliament prescribes by law.
2. The Court originally had ten judges, including the Chief Justice of India.
3. According to Laxmikanth, the Court at present has thirty-four judges: the Chief Justice and thirty-three others.
4. The Number of Judges Amendment Act of 2008 raised the number of other judges to thirty-three.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Parliament, not the Constitution, now sets the number of other judges. Statement 2 is incorrect: The original strength was eight: the CJI and seven others. Ten (CJI plus nine) is not the original number. Statement 3 is correct: The 2019 Amendment Act raised the number of other judges to thirty-three (Laxmikanth ch26 p.414 and Table 26.2). Statement 4 is incorrect: The 2008 Act fixed it at thirty; thirty-three came with the 2019 Act.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.414
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect: p.414
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.414

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the appointment of Judges of the Supreme Court:

1. The Chief Justice of India appoints each judge by a warrant under his hand and seal.
2. For a judge other than the Chief Justice, consultation with the Chief Justice of India is obligatory, while other Supreme Court and High Court judges are consulted as the President deems necessary.
3. The President must consult the Governor of every State before appointing a Supreme Court judge.
4. The consultation requirement was meant to insulate appointments from executive arbitrariness and secure selection on merit.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the President appoints by warrant under his hand and seal (Article 124(2)). Statement 2 is correct: Article 124(2). Statement 3 is incorrect: Governors are consulted for High Court appointments, not for the Supreme Court. Statement 4 is correct: (A16-009).
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.153
'2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.153
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.153

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the qualifications for appointment as a Judge of the Supreme Court:

1. Citizenship of India is the first requirement.
2. Five years of practice as a High Court advocate is enough for eligibility.
3. Five years as a judge of one High Court, or of several in succession, qualifies a person.
4. A person who, in the opinion of the Chief Justice of India, is a distinguished jurist is eligible.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 124(3). Statement 2 is incorrect: ten years as an advocate is required; five years is the High Court judge requirement. Statement 3 is correct: the judicial-experience route. Statement 4 is incorrect: the opinion is that of the President, not of the Chief Justice of India.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the tenure and oath of a Judge of the Supreme Court:

1. A judge holds office until the age of sixty-two years.
2. A judge may resign by a written resignation addressed to the President.
3. The oath requires the judge to bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution and to uphold India's sovereignty and integrity.
4. A judge can be removed by the President acting on the advice of the Chief Justice of India.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: The retirement age of a Supreme Court judge is sixty-five; sixty-two is the High Court age. Statement 2 is correct: Resignation is by writing to the President. Statement 3 is correct: Both pledges are part of the oath. Statement 4 is incorrect: Removal requires an address by each House of Parliament by special majority; the CJI has no such role.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the First Judges Case (1981):

1. It examined the meaning of 'consultation' in Article 124, the balance between the Executive and the Judiciary, and the transfer of High Court judges.
2. It held that the opinion of the Chief Justice of India on appointments was binding on the President.
3. It held that a High Court judge could be transferred to another High Court even against his will.
4. The decision was later widely criticised for weakening judicial independence.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: (A16-016). Statement 2 is incorrect: consultation was held not to mean concurrence, so the CJI's opinion was not binding. Statement 3 is correct: the Court upheld transfer without consent. Statement 4 is correct: (A16-020).
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.153
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.153
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.153

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Second Judges Case (1993):

1. The Court overruled its earlier decision in S.P. Gupta.
2. The Court held that 'consultation' means 'concurrence', so the President is bound by the CJI's advice.
3. The Chief Justice of India was required to consult his three senior-most colleagues.
4. The Court ruled that the senior-most judge alone should be appointed Chief Justice of India.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: It was a complete reversal of the First Judges Case. Statement 2 is correct: Primacy of the CJI's opinion was established (Laxmikanth ch26 p.414). Statement 3 is incorrect: The requirement was two senior-most colleagues; four came with the 1998 opinion. Statement 4 is correct: Laxmikanth ch26 p.415 records this ruling, which curtailed the government's discretion.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.414
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.414
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.414

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Third Judges Case (1998):

1. The Court held that a recommendation made by the CJI without following the consultation norms is binding on the government.
2. The Court held that the sole opinion of the Chief Justice of India does not constitute the consultation process.
3. The collegium was defined as the Chief Justice of India and the four senior-most judges of the Supreme Court.
4. If two judges of the collegium give an adverse opinion, the Chief Justice of India should not send the recommendation to the government.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Such a recommendation is not binding on the government (Laxmikanth ch26 p.414-415). Statement 2 is correct: Consultation must involve a plurality of judges. Statement 3 is correct: This is the 1998 collegium (Laxmikanth ch26 p.414). Statement 4 is correct: The CJI cannot forward the name in that case.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.414
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.414
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.414

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the collegium arrangement for High Court judges:

1. For appointment of High Court judges the Chief Justice of India consults a collegium of the two senior-most Supreme Court judges.
2. The proposal for appointing a High Court judge is initiated by the Union Law Ministry.
3. For transfer of a High Court judge the CJI consults, in addition to the four senior-most Supreme Court judges, the chief justices of the two High Courts concerned.
4. The Supreme Court has held that a transfer may be used by way of punishment.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: This is the Third Judges Case formula for High Court appointments (Laxmikanth ch34 p.508). Statement 2 is incorrect: The proposal originates with the Chief Justice of the High Court, in consultation with senior judges, and travels through the State and Central governments to the collegium. Statement 3 is correct: Laxmikanth ch34 p.511 gives this composition; the transferring and the receiving High Courts. Statement 4 is incorrect: In 1977 it ruled that transfer is an exceptional measure, only in public interest and not by way of punishment.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.508
'1 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.508
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.508

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about judicial appointments:

1. By established convention the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court is appointed Chief Justice of India.
2. In S.P. Gupta (1981) the Court rejected judicial primacy in appointments and upheld executive dominance.
3. After the 2015 verdict striking down the NJAC, the collegium system was restored and judicial primacy reaffirmed.
4. The consultation requirement in Article 124(2) was intended to secure judicial independence and insulate appointments from executive arbitrariness.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Laxmikanth ch26 p.415. Statement 2 is correct: (A16-018). Statement 3 is correct: (A16-029); Laxmikanth ch26 p.415. Statement 4 is correct: (A16-009).
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.415
'1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.415
'1, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.415

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the growth in the strength of the Supreme Court:

1. The Act of 1956 raised the number of judges other than the Chief Justice to ten.
2. The Amendment Act of 1977 raised the number of other judges to seventeen.
3. The Amendment Act of 1986 raised the number of other judges to thirty.
4. The Amendment Act of 1960 raised the number of other judges to thirteen.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Table 26.2 of Laxmikanth records ten in 1956. Statement 2 is correct: The 1977 Act fixed it at seventeen. Statement 3 is incorrect: The 1986 Act fixed twenty-five; thirty came in 2008. Statement 4 is correct: Thirteen was the 1960 figure. Source: Laxmikanth ch26 p.414 and Table 26.2 (p.426-427). So 3 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only one' is not the right count: exactly 3 of the statements are correct.
'Only two' is not the right count: exactly 3 of the statements are correct.
'All four' is not the right count: exactly 3 of the statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Judges Cases and the tenure of judges:

1. The First Judges Case (1981) is S.P. Gupta v. Union of India.
2. The Constitution prescribes no minimum age for appointment as a Supreme Court judge, but a judge retires at 65.
3. The Second Judges Case upheld the First Judges Case and confirmed executive dominance in appointments.
4. A High Court judge retires at 65, the same age as a Supreme Court judge.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The First Judges Case (1981) is S.P. Gupta v. Union of India. Statement 2 is correct: There is no minimum age for appointment as a Supreme Court judge, and judges retire at 65 (Laxmikanth ch26 p.415). Statement 3 is incorrect: the Second Judges Case overruled S.P. Gupta and established judicial primacy. Statement 4 is incorrect: a High Court judge holds office until 62, lower than the Supreme Court's 65. So exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.
'None' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Supreme Court of India:

1. As the final interpreter of the Constitution, it is described as the guardian and protector of Fundamental Rights.
2. The Court was inaugurated on 26 January 1950 and succeeded the Federal Court of India.
3. Like the United States, India has separate federal and State judiciaries enforcing Central and State laws respectively.
4. Parliament has increased the number of judges over time to cope with rising litigation.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: It ensures uniform constitutional interpretation across India. Statement 2 is incorrect: It was inaugurated on 28 January 1950 (Laxmikanth ch26 p.414). Statement 3 is incorrect: India has an integrated judicial system with one hierarchy enforcing both Central and State laws. Statement 4 is correct: The strength rose from eight to thirty-four. So 2 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'None' is not the right count: exactly 2 of the statements are correct.
'Only three' is not the right count: exactly 2 of the statements are correct.
'All four' is not the right count: exactly 2 of the statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The Second Judges Case (1993) is Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association v. Union of India.
Statement-II: That decision laid the foundation of the collegium system for judicial appointments.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: the 1993 case bears this name. Statement-II is correct: the collegium system began with it. Statement-II tells what the case led to; it does not explain why the case carries that name, so it does not explain Statement-I.
w: This option treats Statement-II as explaining the name of the case; the name comes from the petitioner and has nothing to do with the collegium.
This option treats Statement-II as incorrect; the collegium system did begin with the 1993 case.
This option treats Statement-I as incorrect; the Second Judges Case is the Advocates-on-Record case.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: In the First Judges Case the Supreme Court allowed a High Court judge to be transferred to another High Court even against his will.
Statement-II: In that case the Court held that the opinion of the Chief Justice of India was binding on the President.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct. Statement-II is incorrect. The 1981 Court held that consultation is not concurrence, so the CJI's opinion was not binding; Statement-II describes the 1993 position.
w: Rejected: Statement-II is incorrect.
Rejected: Statement-II is incorrect.
Rejected: Statement-I is correct.

questions.q:
Match the clause of Article 124 in List-I with what it deals with in List-II.

List-I
A. Article 124(2)
B. Article 124(2A)
C. Article 124(3)
D. Article 124(6)

List-II
1. Eligibility conditions of citizenship and five years as a High Court judge, ten years as a High Court advocate, or distinguished jurist
2. Authority and manner of fixing the age are for Parliament to provide by law
3. Oath or affirmation in the form in the Third Schedule
4. Appointment by the President by warrant under hand and seal after consultation with judges
questions.e: A-4: Article 124(2) provides appointment by warrant under hand and seal after consultation. B-2: clause (2A) leaves age to Parliament. C-1: clause (3) lays down qualifications. D-3: clause (6) with the Third Schedule prescribes the oath.
w: Rejected: A and B are swapped; appointment is clause (2), age is clause (2A).
Rejected: C and D are swapped; qualifications are clause (3), oath is clause (6).
Rejected: A and C are swapped; appointment is clause (2), eligibility is clause (3).

concepts.name: Supreme Court: NJAC, service conditions, removal, seat and temporary judges
concepts.description: The NJAC and the Fourth Judges Case, salaries and allowances, the removal procedure, the seat of the Court and acting, ad hoc and retired judges.
concepts.idea: Judges are protected by a hard removal procedure and charged salaries, and the Court has provisions for temporary judges.
concepts.rule: The 99th Amendment and the NJAC Act (2014) were struck down in 2015 by a five-judge bench. Salaries are fixed by Parliament and charged on the Consolidated Fund of India. Removal is by the President on an address of each House by a special majority for proved misbehaviour or incapacity, under the Judges (Inquiry) Act 1968: notice by 100 Lok Sabha or 50 Rajya Sabha members, a three-member committee, and a vote in both Houses. Delhi is the seat (Article 130); Articles 126, 127 and 128 provide an acting CJI, ad hoc judges and retired judges.
concepts.example: A removal motion needs 100 Lok Sabha signatures, whereas a request for a retired judge needs the President's consent.

questions.q: The 99th Constitutional Amendment and the NJAC Act of 2014 sought to replace the collegium with a six-member commission. Which one of the following persons was NOT a member of that commission?
o: The Union Minister in charge of Law and Justice
The two senior-most Supreme Court judges next to the Chief Justice of India
Two eminent persons nominated by a committee including the Prime Minister
questions.e: The NJAC had the CJI, two senior-most Supreme Court judges, the Union Law Minister and two eminent persons. The Attorney General had no seat on it. The Supreme Court struck the Act and the amendment down in 2015.
w: He was an ex officio member of the commission.
They were members alongside the CJI, who chaired it.
They were members, chosen by a committee of the PM, the CJI and the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: A litigant petitions a court to direct the Chief Justice of India to hold regular sittings of the Supreme Court at another city. Which one of the following is the correct constitutional position?
questions.a: The petition cannot succeed because appointing another seat is optional for the CJI and needs the President's approval
o: The petition cannot succeed because appointing another seat is optional for the CJI and needs the President's approval
The petition succeeds because Article 130 obliges the CJI to hold sittings in every State capital by rotation
The petition succeeds because the High Court can direct the CJI once two-thirds of judges of the Supreme Court agree
The petition fails because the Governor of the State concerned has not given his consent to shifting the seat of the Court there
questions.e: Article 130 declares Delhi the seat and lets the CJI appoint other places only with the President's approval. The provision is optional, so no court can direct either authority (Laxmikanth ch26 p.417).
w: Article 130 imposes no such obligation; Delhi is the seat.
No court can direct the CJI or the President on this.
The approval needed is the President's, not a Governor's.

questions.q: The Supreme Court lacks a quorum of permanent judges to hold a session. Which one of the following courses is provided by the Constitution?
questions.a: The CJI, after consulting the High Court's Chief Justice and with the President's consent, appoints a qualified High Court judge ad hoc
o: The CJI, after consulting the High Court's Chief Justice and with the President's consent, appoints a qualified High Court judge ad hoc
The President appoints a High Court judge as ad hoc judge on his own, without consulting either the CJI or the Chief Justice of the High Court concerned
The CJI appoints any High Court judge as ad hoc judge on his own authority, and the President's consent is not needed for such an appointment
Parliament must pass a law each time to authorise temporary judges for the Supreme Court, since the Constitution is silent on the matter
questions.e: Article 127 provides for ad hoc judges. The High Court judge must be qualified for appointment to the Supreme Court and must attend its sittings in priority to other duties (Laxmikanth ch26 p.417).
w: The CJI makes the appointment after consulting the High Court Chief Justice, with the President's prior consent.
The previous consent of the President is required.
Article 127 itself empowers the CJI; no law is needed each time.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the financial position of Supreme Court judges is correct?
questions.a: Their salaries and allowances are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India and cannot be voted upon by Parliament
o: Their salaries and allowances are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India and cannot be voted upon by Parliament
Their salaries are exempt from income tax so that no executive authority can reduce their real income through taxation
Their allowances and pension can be reduced to their disadvantage after appointment by an ordinary law of Parliament
A retired judge receives a pension equal to the whole of the last drawn salary, as fixed by the Second Schedule
questions.e: Salaries and allowances are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India, so Parliament may discuss but not vote on them. Pension is 50 per cent of the last salary and salaries are taxable. Also Laxmikanth ch26 p.415-418.
w: The salaries are taxable under the Income Tax Act, 1961.
They cannot be varied to the judges' disadvantage except in a financial emergency.
The pension is fifty per cent of the last drawn salary.

questions.q: A notice of a motion for the removal of a Supreme Court judge must be signed by at least
questions.a: 100 members of the Lok Sabha or 50 members of the Rajya Sabha
o: 100 members of the Lok Sabha or 50 members of the Rajya Sabha
50 members of the Lok Sabha or 100 members of the Rajya Sabha
one-tenth of the total membership of the House in which it is moved
25 members of the Lok Sabha or 10 members of the Rajya Sabha
questions.e: Under the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968 the notice needs 100 Lok Sabha or 50 Rajya Sabha members, which prevents frivolous motions. Laxmikanth ch26 p.416.
w: The figures are reversed.
No fractional threshold applies; fixed numbers do.
These numbers are too low.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the NJAC and the Fourth Judges Case:

1. The 99th Amendment and the NJAC Act of 2014 were intended to replace the collegium system.
2. The 2015 verdict was given by a five-judge Constitution Bench.
3. The Court struck down the NJAC Act but left the 99th Amendment intact.
4. Following the 2015 judgment the collegium was revived.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Both were enacted in 2014 for that purpose. Statement 2 is correct: the 2015 verdict was given by a five-judge Constitution Bench, which struck down the NJAC for violating independence and the basic structure. Statement 3 is incorrect: Both the Amendment and the Act were declared unconstitutional and void (Laxmikanth ch26 p.415). Statement 4 is correct: Judicial primacy was reaffirmed.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.154
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.154
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.154

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the composition of the NJAC:

1. It consisted of the CJI and the three senior-most Supreme Court judges.
2. The Union Law Minister was a member.
3. The two eminent persons were nominated by a committee of the Prime Minister, the CJI and the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha.
4. A recommendation could be blocked if three members opposed it.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: It had the CJI and two senior-most judges. Statement 2 is correct: He sat along with two eminent persons. Statement 3 is correct: That was the nominating committee. Statement 4 is incorrect: It could be blocked if any two members opposed it.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the service conditions of Supreme Court judges:

1. Article 125(1) empowers Parliament to fix their salaries by law, with the Second Schedule applying until then.
2. Their allowances, leave and pension are determined by the President by order without any law.
3. They receive a sumptuary allowance but must provide their own residence.
4. The Supreme Court Judges (Salaries and Conditions of Service) Act, 1958 governs their salaries, leave and pension.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 125(1). Statement 2 is incorrect: Article 125(2) says by or under a law made by Parliament. Statement 3 is incorrect: free official accommodation is among the statutory facilities. Statement 4 is correct: Parliament can revise the terms by amending it.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the removal of a Supreme Court judge:

1. The grounds are proved misbehaviour, incapacity or insolvency.
2. Each House must pass the address by a majority of its total membership and two-thirds of those present and voting.
3. The address may be presented to the President in any later session.
4. Mere allegations are insufficient; misbehaviour or incapacity must be proved by the prescribed procedure.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: only proved misbehaviour or incapacity are grounds. Statement 2 is correct: the special majority, applied separately in each House. Statement 3 is incorrect: Laxmikanth ch26 p.416: it must be presented in the same session. Statement 4 is correct: Article 124(4).
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.416
'1 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.416
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.416

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the procedure for removal of a Supreme Court judge:

1. The motion can be initiated in either the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha.
2. The notice is addressed to the President, who forwards it to the Speaker or Chairman.
3. The Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968 was enacted by Parliament under Article 124(5).
4. The Constitution leaves the procedure for presenting the address and investigating misbehaviour to the Supreme Court's own rules.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The motion can be initiated in either the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha. Statement 2 is incorrect: the notice goes directly to the Speaker or the Chairman. Statement 3 is correct: clause (5) lets Parliament regulate the procedure. Statement 4 is incorrect: Article 124(5) leaves it to Parliament by law.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.156
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.156
'3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.156

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the inquiry stage of a removal motion:

1. On admitting the motion the Speaker or Chairman constitutes a three-member committee of a CJI or Supreme Court judge, a High Court Chief Justice and a distinguished jurist.
2. The committee reports to the Speaker or Chairman of the House where the motion originated, and the report is laid before that House.
3. If misconduct is found proved the House takes up the motion, which must pass by special majority in one House and then the other.
4. After both Houses adopt it the President issues the order, and the judge ceases to hold office from the date of that order.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: That is the composition. Statement 2 is correct: It goes to the same House. Statement 3 is correct: Both Houses must adopt it. Statement 4 is correct: The President acts on the address.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'2, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Justice V. Ramaswami:

1. His case (1991-1993) was the first attempt at impeaching a Supreme Court judge.
2. The inquiry committee cleared him of the charges.
3. The motion was defeated in the Lok Sabha because the Congress party abstained.
4. No Supreme Court judge has been removed from office till now, according to Laxmikanth.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: It is the first such case. Statement 2 is incorrect: The committee found him guilty of misbehaviour. Statement 3 is correct: He therefore could not be removed. Statement 4 is correct: Security of tenure is evident from this.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the seat and the Chief Justice:

1. Article 130 declares Delhi as the seat of the Supreme Court.
2. Article 128 provides for the appointment of an acting Chief Justice of India.
3. An ad hoc judge must attend sittings in priority to other duties and has the powers and privileges of a Supreme Court judge while serving.
4. The CJI may appoint another place as seat of the Court without the President's approval.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The CJI may add other places. Statement 2 is incorrect: Article 126 deals with the acting CJI; Article 128 is about retired judges. Statement 3 is correct: That is the rule under Article 127. Statement 4 is incorrect: The President's prior approval is needed.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Article 128 arrangement for retired judges:

1. The CJI may request a retired Supreme Court judge, or a retired High Court judge qualified to be a Supreme Court judge, to act as a judge.
2. It needs the previous consent of the President and of the retired judge.
3. Such a judge gets allowances fixed by the President and all jurisdiction, powers and privileges of a Supreme Court judge while sitting.
4. He is thereby deemed a regular Supreme Court judge for all other purposes.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: That is Article 128. Statement 2 is correct: Both consents are required. Statement 3 is correct: The allowances are determined by the President. Statement 4 is incorrect: Laxmikanth ch26 p.417: he is not otherwise deemed to be a judge of the Court.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.417
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.417
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.417

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the law governing removal of judges:

1. Article 124(5) authorises Parliament to regulate presentation of the address and the investigation and proof of misbehaviour or incapacity.
2. The Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968 and the Judges (Inquiry) Rules, 1969 lay down the procedure.
3. The Judges (Inquiry) Act applies to High Court judges but not to Supreme Court judges.
4. The word 'impeachment' is used in the Constitution for the removal of Supreme Court judges.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: That is the source of the procedure. Statement 2 is correct: Both exist. Statement 3 is incorrect: It covers Supreme Court judges as well. Statement 4 is incorrect: The Constitution uses the word only for the President (Laxmikanth ch26 fn.6). So 2 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only one' is not the right count: exactly 2 of the statements are correct.
'Only three' is not the right count: exactly 2 of the statements are correct.
'All four' is not the right count: exactly 2 of the statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the temporary arrangements for the Supreme Court:

1. The High Court judge appointed ad hoc must be qualified for appointment as a Supreme Court judge.
2. The CJI must consult the Chief Justice of the High Court concerned before appointing him.
3. Under Article 126 the President may appoint a Supreme Court judge as acting Chief Justice when the office is vacant or the CJI is unable to perform his duties.
4. An ad hoc judge need not attend Supreme Court sittings in priority to his High Court duties.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 127. Statement 2 is correct: consultation is mandatory. Statement 3 is correct: Article 126. Statement 4 is incorrect: he must attend in priority over other duties. So exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.
'None' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the independence of Supreme Court judges:

1. A retired Chief Justice and judges get a pension equal to two-thirds of the last drawn salary.
2. Their salaries are subject to an annual vote of the Lok Sabha.
3. Their service conditions cannot be varied to their disadvantage after appointment, except in a financial emergency.
4. Retired judges may plead before High Courts although not before the Supreme Court.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: It is fifty per cent. Statement 2 is incorrect: They are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India and non-votable. Statement 3 is correct: Laxmikanth ch26 p.415. Statement 4 is incorrect: They are barred from pleading before any court or authority in India (Laxmikanth ch26 p.418). So 1 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only two' is not the right count: exactly 1 of the statements is correct.
'Only three' is not the right count: exactly 1 of the statements is correct.
'All four' is not the right count: exactly 1 of the statements is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: A Supreme Court judge cannot be removed by the executive acting alone.
Statement-II: Removal needs an address by each House of Parliament passed by a special majority.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct. Statement-II is correct. The parliamentary address is the safeguard that stops the executive acting alone, so Statement-II explains Statement-I.
w: Rejected: Statement-II is the very reason for Statement-I, so it does explain it.
Rejected: Statement-II is correct.
Rejected: Statement-I is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: A notice of a motion to remove a Supreme Court judge needs 100 Lok Sabha or 50 Rajya Sabha members.
Statement-II: The Speaker or Chairman has no discretion to reject a motion once the required number of members has signed.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct. Statement-II is incorrect. The Speaker or Chairman examines the material and may admit or reject the motion.
w: Rejected: Statement-II is incorrect.
Rejected: Statement-II is incorrect.
Rejected: Statement-I is correct.

questions.q:
Match the Article in List-I with the provision it makes in List-II.

List-I
A. Article 126
B. Article 127
C. Article 128
D. Article 130

List-II
1. Seat of the Supreme Court
2. Acting Chief Justice of India
3. Request to retired judges to sit as judges
4. Ad hoc judges for lack of quorum
questions.e: A-2: Article 126 acting CJI. B-4: Article 127 ad hoc judges. C-3: Article 128 retired judges. D-1: Article 130 seat.
w: Rejected: A and B are swapped.
Rejected: B and C are swapped.
Rejected: C and D are swapped.

concepts.name: Supreme Court jurisdiction and the High Court table
concepts.description: Original, writ, appellate, advisory and record powers of the Supreme Court, contempt, and the establishment, seats and jurisdiction of the High Courts.
concepts.idea: The Supreme Court has several kinds of jurisdiction, and each High Court has its own year, seat and territory.
concepts.rule: Article 131 gives exclusive original jurisdiction in Centre-State and inter-State disputes, with exclusions. Article 32 writs are for Fundamental Rights; Articles 132 to 136 give appeals; Article 143 an advisory opinion by a Bench of five or more judges. Article 129 makes it a court of record; contempt is civil or criminal. High Courts began in 1862 at Calcutta, Bombay and Madras; Article 214 gives one per State and the Seventh Amendment allowed common High Courts. Laxmikanth lists 25 High Courts with years, seats and benches.
concepts.example: A dispute between a State and the Centre goes straight to the Supreme Court, but a Kolkata person approaches the Calcutta High Court.

questions.q: Which one of the following disputes can be taken directly to the Supreme Court under its exclusive original jurisdiction in Article 131?
questions.a: A dispute between the Union and a State over whether a Central Act infringes a legal right of the State
o: A dispute between the Union and a State over whether a Central Act infringes a legal right of the State
A suit by a private company against a State government over a supply contract it signed with that State government
A dispute between two States over the use of the water of an inter-State river flowing through both
A matter that the Constitution refers to the Finance Commission for its recommendation
questions.e: Article 131 covers Centre-State, Centre and States against other States, and inter-State disputes involving a question of law or fact on which a legal right depends. Exclusions: pre-Constitution treaties, water disputes, Finance Commission matters and adjustment of certain expenses and pensions. Laxmikanth ch26 p.419-420.
w: A suit by a private citizen or company cannot be entertained under Article 131.
Inter-State water disputes are excluded (Article 262 and the 1956 Act).
Matters referred to the Finance Commission are excluded from Article 131.

questions.q: Which one of the following is correct about the writ jurisdiction of the Supreme Court under Article 32?
questions.a: It is confined to Fundamental Rights, though Parliament may by law confer writ power for other purposes
o: It is confined to Fundamental Rights, though Parliament may by law confer writ power for other purposes
It is exclusive, so High Courts cannot issue writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights at all in their territories
It extends to any ordinary legal right and so is wider than the writ power of a High Court
It can be invoked only by way of appeal from a High Court judgment refusing relief
questions.e: Article 32 gives original, non-exclusive writ power for Fundamental Rights; Article 139 lets Parliament confer wider writ power. Laxmikanth ch26 p.420.
w: High Courts have concurrent power under Article 226.
The High Court's power is wider; the Supreme Court's is confined to Fundamental Rights.
An aggrieved person may go directly to the Supreme Court.

questions.q: Special leave to appeal under Article 136 can be granted by the Supreme Court against
questions.a: a judgment of any court or tribunal in the country, other than those relating to the armed forces
o: a judgment of any court or tribunal in the country, other than those relating to the armed forces
only a judgment of a High Court, after the High Court has refused to grant a certificate of appeal
only a final judgment of a court, and not an interlocutory order passed in the course of a case
a decision of a court martial, which the Court must hear as a matter of right
questions.e: Article 136 is a discretionary, extraordinary power giving the Court residual appellate authority over any court or tribunal except military ones. Laxmikanth ch26 p.421.
w: Special leave lies against any court or tribunal, not only a High Court.
Laxmikanth ch26 p.421: it may be granted against a final or interlocutory judgment.
Military tribunals and courts martial are excluded, and the power is discretionary.

questions.q: The power of Parliament to establish a common High Court for two or more States, or for States and a Union Territory, was provided by
questions.e: The Seventh Amendment (1956) authorised common High Courts (Article 231), along with reorganisation by linguistic States. Article 214 provides a High Court for each State. Laxmikanth ch34 p.508.
w: That Act raised the retirement age of High Court judges to 62.
That Act curtailed the judicial review power of High Courts over Central laws.
That Act dealt with Parliament's power to amend the Constitution.

questions.q: Which one of the following amounts to civil contempt under the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971?
questions.a: Wilful breach of an undertaking given to a court
o: Wilful breach of an undertaking given to a court
A publication that scandalises or lowers the authority of a court
An act that interferes with the due course of a judicial proceeding
A fair and accurate report of judicial proceedings
questions.e: Civil contempt is wilful disobedience of a judgment, decree, order, writ or other process, or breach of an undertaking; its object is to enforce court orders, not to punish criticism. Criminal contempt is scandalising, prejudicing proceedings or obstructing justice. Laxmikanth ch26 p.423.
w: That is criminal contempt.
That is criminal contempt.
It is expressly not contempt.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 131:

1. Disputes between the Centre and States, and among States, fall in the exclusive original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.
2. A suit by a private citizen against a State can be brought under it.
3. Disputes arising from pre-Constitution treaties that continue in operation are excluded.
4. Inter-State water disputes and matters referred to the Finance Commission are excluded.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Three kinds of disputes are covered. Statement 2 is incorrect: Private citizens cannot invoke Article 131. Statement 3 is correct: They fall outside Article 131. Statement 4 is correct: Under Articles 262 and 280 respectively.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 2, which is incorrect

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court:

1. A constitutional appeal from a High Court requires a certificate of a substantial question of interpretation.
2. The monetary limit of Rs 20,000 for civil appeals still applies.
3. An appeal to the Supreme Court needs no certificate where a High Court overturned an acquittal and imposed the death sentence.
4. An appeal lies as of right where a High Court reversed a conviction and ordered acquittal.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 132; Laxmikanth ch26 p.421. Statement 2 is incorrect: The 30th Amendment of 1972 removed it. Statement 3 is correct: Article 134 and Laxmikanth ch26 p.421. Statement 4 is incorrect: There is no right of appeal in that case.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.421
'3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.421
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.421

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Supreme Court:

1. The President may consult the Court under Article 143 on a question of law or fact of public importance that has arisen or may arise.
2. It is the highest court of appeal in India.
3. Its advisory opinion is binding on the President.
4. Advisory opinions are delivered by a bench of at least three judges.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 143. Statement 2 is correct: it replaced the Privy Council. Statement 3 is incorrect: the opinion is advisory only. Statement 4 is incorrect: a Constitution Bench of at least five judges (Laxmikanth ch26 p.417).
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.417
'2 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.417
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.417

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about contempt of court:

1. The records of the Supreme Court as a court of record are of evidentiary value and cannot be questioned before any court.
2. The Supreme Court can punish the contempt of itself but not of High Courts or subordinate courts.
3. No court shall initiate contempt proceedings after one year from the alleged contempt.
4. Nyaya Panchayats and other village courts fall within the 1971 contempt law.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 129; Laxmikanth ch26 p.423. Statement 2 is incorrect: In 1991 it held it can punish contempt of High Courts, subordinate courts and tribunals. Statement 3 is correct: Laxmikanth ch26 p.423. Statement 4 is incorrect: It does not apply to them.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.423
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.423
'1 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.423

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the powers of the Supreme Court:

1. Under Article 141 the law declared by it is binding on all courts in India.
2. Under Article 142 it can pass any decree or order necessary to do complete justice.
3. Article 144 requires executive authorities, but not judicial authorities, to act in aid of it.
4. As the final interpreter it can declare void a law that violates the Fundamental Rights, but not one that violates the basic structure.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 141. Statement 2 is correct: Article 142. Statement 3 is incorrect: all civil and judicial authorities must act in aid. Statement 4 is incorrect: laws violating Fundamental Rights or the basic structure can be declared void.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'2 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the review and other powers of the Supreme Court:

1. A review petition must be filed within ninety days of the judgment.
2. A curative petition may be entertained after a review petition is dismissed, on limited grounds.
3. It can transfer a case from one High Court to another.
4. Its jurisdiction on Union List matters can be enlarged by Parliament.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Thirty days (Laxmikanth ch26 p.424). Statement 2 is correct: Laxmikanth ch26 p.424. Statement 3 is correct: Laxmikanth ch26 p.425. Statement 4 is correct: Laxmikanth ch26 p.425.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.424
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.424
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.424

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about High Courts:

1. A High Court is the apex judicial authority at State level and supervises subordinate courts.
2. Article 214 provides a common High Court for two or more States.
3. A common High Court for States and Union Territories is provided by Article 231.
4. The High Courts originated at Calcutta, Bombay and Madras in 1862.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Below the Supreme Court, above subordinate courts. Statement 2 is incorrect: Article 214 provides one for each State; common High Courts come under Article 231. Statement 3 is correct: The Seventh Amendment enabled it. Statement 4 is correct: Allahabad followed in 1866 (Laxmikanth ch34 p.508).
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.508
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.508
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.508

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the establishment of High Courts:

1. Port Blair and Jalpaiguri host circuit benches of the Calcutta High Court, which was established in 1862.
2. The Allahabad High Court dates from 1866 and has a bench at Lucknow.
3. The Andhra Pradesh High Court was established in 2019 with its seat at Amaravati.
4. The Delhi High Court was established in 1966 for the NCT of Delhi.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Laxmikanth Table 34.1 lists both circuit benches. Statement 2 is correct: It was the fourth High Court. Statement 3 is correct: A separate High Court for the State came up in 2019. Statement 4 is correct: Delhi alone among Union Territories has its own High Court (Laxmikanth ch34 p.508).
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.508
'2, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.508
'1, 2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.508

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the establishment of High Courts:

1. The Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand and Uttarakhand High Courts were all established in 2001.
2. The Manipur, Meghalaya and Tripura High Courts were all established in 2013.
3. The Gujarat High Court was established in 1971 and the Himachal Pradesh High Court in 1960.
4. The Orissa High Court dates from 1948 with its seat at Bhubaneswar.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: they were established in 2000 with the three new States. Statement 2 is correct: separate courts for the three north-eastern States. Statement 3 is incorrect: the years are swapped: Gujarat 1960, Himachal Pradesh 1971. Statement 4 is incorrect: its seat is Cuttack, and its name was not changed to Odisha.
w: '3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect
'4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about High Court seats and benches:

1. The Karnataka High Court sits at Bengaluru with benches at Dharwad and Gulbarga.
2. Madurai hosts a bench of the Madras High Court.
3. Jaipur is the principal seat of the Rajasthan High Court, established in 1949, which also holds a bench at Jodhpur.
4. The Kerala High Court (1956) sits at Ernakulam and the Madhya Pradesh High Court (1956) at Jabalpur with benches at Gwalior and Indore.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Laxmikanth Table 34.1. Statement 2 is correct: Table 34.1. Statement 3 is incorrect: The seat is Jodhpur and the bench is at Jaipur. Statement 4 is correct: Both were established in 1956. So 3 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only one' is not the right count: exactly 3 of the statements are correct.
'Only two' is not the right count: exactly 3 of the statements are correct.
'All four' is not the right count: exactly 3 of the statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the territorial jurisdiction of High Courts:

1. Goa, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu lie within the territorial jurisdiction of the Bombay High Court, along with Maharashtra.
2. The Gauhati High Court covers Assam, Nagaland, Manipur and Arunachal Pradesh.
3. Chandigarh is both within the territorial jurisdiction and the seat of the Punjab and Haryana High Court.
4. The Madras High Court covers Tamil Nadu and Lakshadweep.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: One of three multi-State courts. Statement 2 is incorrect: It covers Assam, Nagaland, Mizoram and Arunachal Pradesh; Manipur has its own. Statement 3 is correct: Seat Chandigarh. Statement 4 is incorrect: It covers Tamil Nadu and Puducherry. So 2 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'None' is not the right count: exactly 2 of the statements are correct.
'Only one' is not the right count: exactly 2 of the statements are correct.
'Only three' is not the right count: exactly 2 of the statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Union Territories and High Courts:

1. Lakshadweep falls under the Kerala High Court.
2. Puducherry falls under the Karnataka High Court.
3. Chandigarh falls under the Delhi High Court.
4. The Andaman and Nicobar Islands fall under the Madras High Court.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Per the chapter. Statement 2 is incorrect: It falls under Madras. Statement 3 is incorrect: Under Punjab and Haryana. Statement 4 is incorrect: Under Calcutta. India has 25 High Courts according to Laxmikanth ch34 p.508; Delhi alone among UTs has its own. So 1 statement(s) are correct.

'Only three' is not the right count: exactly 1 of the statements is correct.
'All four' is not the right count: exactly 1 of the statements is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: An advisory opinion of the Supreme Court under Article 143 does not bind the President.
Statement-II: Such an opinion is not a judicial pronouncement.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct. Statement-II is correct. Because it is only advisory and not a judicial pronouncement, the President may or may not follow it (Laxmikanth ch26 p.422).
w: Rejected: Statement-II is the very reason for Statement-I, so it does explain it.
Rejected: Statement-II is correct.
Rejected: Statement-I is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The Supreme Court can issue writs under Article 32 only for enforcing Fundamental Rights.
Statement-II: Under Article 139 Parliament may by law give the Supreme Court extra writ power for purposes other than Fundamental Rights.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct. Statement-II is correct. Statement-II is a separate qualification; it does not explain why Article 32 itself is confined to Fundamental Rights.
w: Rejected: Statement-II does not explain Statement-I; it is a separate fact.
Rejected: Statement-II is correct.
Rejected: Statement-I is correct.

questions.q:
Using the table in Laxmikanth, which dates the Telangana High Court from the original Hyderabad court of 1954, pair each High Court in List-I with the year it was established, given in List-II.

List-I
