concepts.name: High Court: composition, appointment, service conditions, removal, temporary judges and original jurisdiction
concepts.description: Composition of a High Court, qualifications, appointment, oath, salaries, resignation, removal, transfer, acting, additional and retired judges and original jurisdiction.
concepts.idea: High Court judges are appointed with wider consultation and retire earlier than Supreme Court judges.
concepts.rule: A High Court has a Chief Justice and judges as the President appoints. A judge is a citizen with ten years of judicial office or ten years as a High Court advocate; there is no jurist route. The CJI, the Governor and the High Court Chief Justice are consulted. Retirement is at 62, the oath is before the Governor, removal is as for the Supreme Court, and Article 222 allows transfer after consulting the CJI. Article 223 acting Chief Justice, Article 224 additional (two years) and acting judges, Article 224A retired judges. Original jurisdiction covers election disputes, revenue matters and Article 226 writs.
concepts.example: A High Court judge transferred to another High Court gets a compensatory allowance, but cannot be punished by transfer.

questions.q: Which one of the following persons is eligible for appointment as a Judge of a High Court?
questions.a: A citizen who has held judicial office in India for ten years and has never practised as an advocate
o: A citizen who has held judicial office in India for ten years and has never practised as an advocate
A distinguished jurist, in the opinion of the President, who has neither held judicial office nor practised
A citizen who has held judicial office in India for seven years and is a member of a higher judicial service
A citizen who has been an advocate of a High Court for five years and has also served as a Government Pleader
questions.e: A High Court judge must be a citizen and either have held judicial office in India for ten years or have been a High Court advocate for ten years. There is no minimum age and no jurist route. Laxmikanth ch34 p.509.
w: There is no distinguished-jurist route for High Courts, unlike the Supreme Court.
Ten years of judicial office is required.
Ten years as an advocate of a High Court is required.

questions.q: For appointment of a High Court judge other than the Chief Justice, the President consults
questions.a: the Chief Justice of India, the State Governor and the Chief Justice of that High Court
o: the Chief Justice of India, the State Governor and the Chief Justice of that High Court
the Chief Justice of India and the Chief Minister of the State concerned, but not the Governor
the Governor and the State Public Service Commission, together with the Law Secretary of the State
the Chief Justice of the High Court and the Governor, without consulting the Chief Justice of India
questions.e: The President consults the CJI, the Governor and, for a judge other than the Chief Justice, the Chief Justice of the High Court. The Governor's role is consultative, not determinative. Laxmikanth ch34 p.508.
w: The Chief Minister has no constitutional consultative role; the Governor and the High Court Chief Justice are consulted.
The Public Service Commission is consulted for subordinate judicial service, not High Court judges.
Consultation with the Chief Justice of India is mandatory.

questions.q: Raising the superannuation age of High Court judges from 60 to 62 was the work of
questions.e: A High Court judge holds office until 62, lower than the 65 of a Supreme Court judge. The age was raised from 60 by the 15th Amendment of 1963 (Laxmikanth ch34 p.510).
w: That Act authorised common High Courts.
That Act curtailed High Courts' power to consider the validity of Central laws.
That Act deleted entries from the Ninth Schedule, among other things; it did not change judges' age.

questions.q: When a judge is moved from one High Court to another, which one of the following is correct?
questions.a: The President transfers him after consulting the Chief Justice of India, and he gets a compensatory allowance
o: The President transfers him after consulting the Chief Justice of India, and he gets a compensatory allowance
The Governor transfers him with the consent of the Chief Justice of the receiving High Court, and no extra allowance is paid to him
The Chief Justice of India transfers him by an administrative order without involving the President or any consultation
Parliament transfers him by a resolution passed by a special majority of the members present and voting in each House
questions.e: Article 222(1) lets the President transfer a judge after consulting the CJI; the compensatory allowance is fixed by Parliament by law (or by the President's order until a law exists). Laxmikanth ch34 p.510.
w: The transfer power is the President's under Article 222.
The order is the President's, after consulting the CJI.
Parliament has no role in an individual transfer.

questions.q: A permanent judge of a High Court, who is not the Chief Justice, goes on long leave. Which appointment may the President make to carry on the work?
questions.a: An acting judge, who holds office until the permanent judge resumes
o: An acting judge, who holds office until the permanent judge resumes
An additional judge for a term not exceeding two years
An acting Chief Justice under Article 223
A judge transferred permanently from another High Court under Article 222
questions.e: Article 224(2) provides acting judges for absence or inability of a judge other than the Chief Justice. Laxmikanth ch34 p.511.
w: Additional judges are appointed for a temporary increase in business or arrears, not for a judge's absence.
Article 223 applies to vacancy or absence of the Chief Justice.
A transfer is not a temporary substitute and needs consultation with the CJI.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the composition of a High Court:

1. Under Article 216 a High Court consists of a Chief Justice and such other judges as the President appoints from time to time.
2. The Constitution itself fixes the strength of each High Court.
3. According to Laxmikanth the President determines the strength depending upon the workload.
4. The President appoints each judge through a warrant bearing his hand and seal.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: That is the composition rule. Statement 2 is incorrect: The strength is left to the President. Statement 3 is correct: Laxmikanth ch34 p.508. Statement 4 is correct: After the prescribed consultation.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.508
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.508
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.508

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the qualifications of a High Court judge:

1. Indian citizenship is a precondition.
2. Ten years of judicial office in India qualifies, including service as a district judge.
3. A person who is a distinguished jurist in the opinion of the President is also eligible.
4. The Constitution prescribes no minimum age, only retirement at 62.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Citizenship is required. Statement 2 is correct: One route. Statement 3 is incorrect: That route exists only for the Supreme Court. Statement 4 is correct: No minimum age.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 3, which is incorrect

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the appointment process of High Court judges:

1. The opinion of the CJI is to be treated as his unilateral discretion.
2. In practice the proposal is initiated by the Chief Justice of the High Court concerned and not by the executive.
3. The consultation required by Article 217(1) is mandatory, and a mere formality does not satisfy it.
4. Under the collegium system, if the collegium reiterates a recommendation, the Government remains free to reject it again.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: it must reflect collective judicial wisdom. Statement 2 is correct: (A16-149). Statement 3 is correct: (A16-150). Statement 4 is incorrect: on reiteration the executive is bound to act (A16-151).
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.161
'2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.161
'2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.161

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about oath, pay and resignation of High Court judges:

1. A High Court judge makes the oath or affirmation before the Governor or a person he appoints.
2. Salaries are fixed by the State Legislature by law.
3. Allowances, leave and pension are determined by Parliament and until altered are governed by the Second Schedule.
4. A judge resigns by writing to the Governor.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 219. Statement 2 is incorrect: Parliament fixes them; the Second Schedule applies until then. Statement 3 is correct: Article 221(2). Statement 4 is incorrect: He writes to the President.
w: '1 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the removal of a High Court judge:

1. The President removes him only on a recommendation of Parliament and not at his own discretion.
2. The grounds are proved misbehaviour and proved incapacity.
3. The special majority and judicial inquiry are the same as for a Supreme Court judge.
4. The removal motion is moved in the Lok Sabha, the Rajya Sabha having no role.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Parliament's address is needed. Statement 2 is correct: Two grounds. Statement 3 is correct: Procedure is the same. Statement 4 is incorrect: Either House may initiate it.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the transfer of High Court judges:

1. The President may transfer a judge after consulting the Chief Justice of India.
2. The Supreme Court has held in 1994 that transfers are beyond judicial review.
3. The Supreme Court ruled in 1977 that transfer may be used only as an exceptional measure in public interest.
4. Only the judge who is transferred can challenge it.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 222. Statement 2 is incorrect: It held that review is needed to check arbitrariness. Statement 3 is correct: Not as punishment. Statement 4 is correct: Laxmikanth ch34 p.511.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.511
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.511
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.511

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about temporary judges of High Courts:

1. An acting Chief Justice is appointed under Article 224.
2. An additional judge is appointed for a term of at most two years for workload or arrears.
3. An acting judge serves until the permanent judge returns.
4. A retired judge sitting under Article 224A is deemed a regular judge of the court for all other purposes.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Under Article 223; Article 224 deals with additional and acting judges. Statement 2 is correct: Article 224(1). Statement 3 is correct: A substitute judge. Statement 4 is incorrect: He is not otherwise deemed a judge of that court.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect
'3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the original jurisdiction of a High Court:

1. It means the power to hear a case at first instance, including Article 226 writs for Fundamental Rights and other legal rights.
2. Election disputes of Parliament and State legislature members are filed directly in the High Court.
3. Revenue jurisdiction is an inherited pre-Constitution power merely continued by the Constitution.
4. The original criminal jurisdiction that the Calcutta, Bombay and Madras High Courts once had was ended by the Criminal Procedure Code of 1973 (since replaced by the BNSS).

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Wider than Article 32. Statement 2 is correct: Appeals lie to the Supreme Court. Statement 3 is incorrect: Laxmikanth ch34 p.513: it is an addition not enjoyed before. Statement 4 is correct: Before 1973 they had it.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.513
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.513
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.513

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the jurisdiction of a High Court:

1. It is governed by the Constitution, Acts of Parliament and of State legislatures and the Civil Procedure Code 1908, and for the chartered High Courts also by their Letters Patent.
2. Admiralty jurisdiction relates to maritime disputes such as arrest of ships and maritime contracts.
3. A High Court may take over from a subordinate court a case involving a substantial question of constitutional interpretation.
4. The power to punish contempt under Article 215 forms part of its original, not appellate, jurisdiction.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Among the sources. Statement 2 is correct: Admiralty jurisdiction covers maritime disputes such as the arrest of ships and maritime contracts. Statement 3 is correct: Laxmikanth ch34 p.513. Statement 4 is correct: Article 215 makes it a court of record.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.513
'1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.513
'1, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.513

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the tenure of High Court judges:

1. A High Court judge holds office until the age of 62.
2. The President, after consulting the CJI, finally decides any dispute about a judge's age.
3. Neither an additional nor an acting judge may continue beyond the age of 62.
4. The retirement age is the same as that of a Supreme Court judge.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Lower than 65. Statement 2 is correct: Laxmikanth ch34 p.510. Statement 3 is correct: Laxmikanth ch34 p.511. Statement 4 is incorrect: 65 versus 62. So 3 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only one' is not the right count: exactly 3 of the statements are correct.
'Only two' is not the right count: exactly 3 of the statements are correct.
'All four' is not the right count: exactly 3 of the statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about High Court judges:

1. The office is vacated automatically on elevation to the Supreme Court.
2. A judge transferred under Article 222 continues to hold his earlier post in the old High Court.
3. The compensatory allowance of a transferred judge is fixed by the Governor.
4. The Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968 does not apply to High Court judges.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Prevents holding two offices. Statement 2 is incorrect: He vacates it. Statement 3 is incorrect: By Parliament or the President's order. Statement 4 is incorrect: It covers High Court judges too. So 1 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'None' is not the right count: exactly 1 of the statements is correct.
'Only two' is not the right count: exactly 1 of the statements is correct.
'Only three' is not the right count: exactly 1 of the statements is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the independence of High Courts:

1. The State's Consolidated Fund bears the salaries and allowances of High Court judges.
2. A High Court judge's pension is paid from the Consolidated Fund of the State.
3. A retired permanent judge may practise before the Supreme Court and other High Courts.
4. The conduct of a High Court judge may be freely discussed in the State legislature.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Laxmikanth ch34 p.512. Statement 2 is incorrect: Of India. Statement 3 is correct: Not before the court he retired from. Statement 4 is incorrect: Prohibited except impeachment. So 2 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'None' is not the right count: exactly 2 of the statements are correct.
'Only three' is not the right count: exactly 2 of the statements are correct.
'All four' is not the right count: exactly 2 of the statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: Four High Courts, namely Calcutta, Bombay, Madras and Delhi, can try high-value civil suits as courts of first instance.
Statement-II: Calcutta, Bombay and Madras lost their original criminal jurisdiction when the Criminal Procedure Code of 1973 came into force.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct. Statement-II is correct. The two facts are separate; the abolition of criminal jurisdiction does not explain civil jurisdiction.
w: Rejected: Statement-II does not explain Statement-I; it is a separate fact.
Rejected: Statement-II is correct.
Rejected: Statement-I is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: An acting Chief Justice of a High Court is appointed under Article 223 for a vacancy or the absence of the Chief Justice.
Statement-II: An acting judge under Article 224(2) is appointed for the temporary absence of a regular judge.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: Article 223 deals with the acting Chief Justice. Statement-II is correct: Article 224(2) provides acting judges. They are two separate temporary arrangements; neither explains the other.
w: This option treats Statement-II as explaining Statement-I; the two provisions cover different posts.
This option treats Statement-II as incorrect; Article 224(2) does provide acting judges for absence.
This option treats Statement-I as incorrect; Article 223 provides for an acting Chief Justice.

questions.q:
Match the Article in List-I with what it provides in List-II.

List-I
A. Article 216
B. Article 219
C. Article 221
D. Article 224A

List-II
1. Salaries fixed by Parliament by law
2. Composition of High Courts
3. Calling retired judges to sit temporarily
4. Oath before the Governor
questions.e: 216 composition, 219 oath, 221 salaries, 224A retired judges.
w: Rejected: A and B swapped.
Rejected: C and D swapped.
Rejected: A and C swapped.

concepts.name: High Court: writs, appeals, superintendence, control over subordinate courts, court of record and judicial review
concepts.description: Article 226 writs, appellate jurisdiction, Article 227 superintendence, Articles 233 to 235 and 228, court of record and judicial review.
concepts.idea: A High Court supervises subordinate courts and its writ power is wider than the Supreme Court's.
concepts.rule: Article 226 allows writs for Fundamental Rights and any other purpose, concurrent with Article 32, and outside the territory if the cause of action arises within. L. Chandra Kumar (1997) made judicial review a basic feature. First appeals lie on law and fact, second appeals on substantial questions of law; sessions appeals lie when the sentence exceeds seven years and a death sentence needs confirmation. Article 227 gives superintendence over all courts and tribunals except military; Article 233 and 234 govern appointment of judges, Article 235 gives control to the High Court.
concepts.example: A District Judge is appointed by the Governor, but disciplined by the High Court.

questions.q: In L. Chandra Kumar v. Union of India (1997), the Supreme Court held that
questions.a: judicial review under Articles 226 and 32 is a basic feature, so tribunals remain under High Court writ jurisdiction
o: judicial review under Articles 226 and 32 is a basic feature, so tribunals remain under High Court writ jurisdiction
Parliament may oust the writ jurisdiction of High Courts over tribunals by an ordinary law, without any constitutional amendment
appeals from the decisions of tribunals lie directly to the Supreme Court, bypassing the High Court altogether
High Courts cannot review tribunal decisions even when a Fundamental Right is involved, since tribunals lie outside them
questions.e: L. Chandra Kumar (1997) made the writ jurisdiction of the High Courts and the Supreme Court part of the basic structure. Hence an appeal against a tribunal normally goes to the High Court division bench, not straight to the Supreme Court. Laxmikanth ch34 p.514.
w: Judicial review under Articles 226 and 32 cannot be ousted even by a constitutional amendment.
An aggrieved person must first approach the High Court.
Tribunals are under the writ jurisdiction of High Courts.

questions.q: An order of a Delhi-based central authority adversely affects a resident of Kerala. Which one of the following is correct about the writ jurisdiction of the Kerala High Court?
questions.a: It can entertain a writ petition because part of the cause of action arises within its territory
o: It can entertain a writ petition because part of the cause of action arises within its territory
It cannot, because writs run only against authorities located within the territory of the High Court
It cannot, because only the Supreme Court can issue a writ against a Central authority
It can, but only if the Delhi High Court first transfers the case
questions.e: Article 226(2), added by the 15th Amendment of 1963, lets a High Court issue writs to any person, authority or government outside its territory if the cause of action arises wholly or partly within it. Laxmikanth ch34 p.514.
w: Article 226 permits writs outside the territory if the cause of action arises within it.
Article 32 is concurrent, not exclusive.
No transfer is required.

questions.q: The power of superintendence of a High Court under Article 227 does not extend to
o: district courts that are not subject to its appellate jurisdiction
quasi-judicial tribunals functioning in its territory
subordinate courts whose decisions are made final by a statute
questions.e: Article 227(1) gives superintendence over all courts and tribunals in the High Court's territory except military ones; it covers administrative and judicial superintendence and can be exercised suo motu. Laxmikanth ch34 p.515.
w: It extends to all courts and tribunals whether or not subject to appeal.
Tribunals are covered.
Statutory finality does not remove superintendence.

questions.q: In State of West Bengal v. Nripendra Nath Bagchi (1966) the Supreme Court held that the word 'control' in Article 235 includes
questions.a: disciplinary control over members of the judicial service, and not merely administrative oversight
o: disciplinary control over members of the judicial service, and not merely administrative oversight
only the power to post and promote district judges, which excludes any power of discipline over them
the power of the Governor to dismiss a judicial officer without any reference to the High Court at all
the power to appoint district judges, which belongs to the High Court acting in its own right
questions.e: Article 235 vests control over district courts and courts below in the High Court; Nripendra Nath Bagchi held it covers discipline. Shamsher Singh (1974) added that the control is the High Court's even though orders issue in the Governor's name.
w: Control was held to include discipline.
Control vests in the High Court.
Appointment of district judges is by the Governor in consultation with the High Court.

questions.q: Which one of the following is a correct statement about judicial review in India?
questions.a: It began in the USA with Marbury v. Madison (1803); in India the Constitution itself confers it on the Supreme Court and High Courts
o: It began in the USA with Marbury v. Madison (1803); in India the Constitution itself confers it on the Supreme Court and High Courts
It originated in the USA, but the Indian Constitution is silent on it and the Supreme Court derived it from the basic structure doctrine
It was first propounded in India in Kesavananda Bharati (1973) and was later adopted in the United States as well
It originated in the USA, but in India the Constitution confers it on the Supreme Court and not on the High Courts
questions.e: Marbury v. Madison (1803), by Chief Justice John Marshall, propounded judicial review. In India Articles 13, 32, 226 and others explicitly confer it on the Supreme Court and High Courts, and it is a basic feature. Laxmikanth ch27 p.431-433.
w: Articles 13, 32, 226 and others explicitly confer it.
It originated in the USA in 1803.
High Courts have it under Articles 13 and 226.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the writ jurisdiction of a High Court under Article 226:

1. It can issue directions, orders or writs for Fundamental Rights and for any other purpose.
2. A petitioner must show breach of a Fundamental Right.
3. Grounds are confined to breach of statutory rules; breach of natural justice falls outside Article 226.
4. It is wider than the Supreme Court's power under Article 32.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 226. Statement 2 is incorrect: an ordinary legal or statutory right suffices. Statement 3 is incorrect: breach of natural justice and ultra vires action are grounds. Statement 4 is correct: Article 32 is limited to Fundamental Rights.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'1 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the High Court and the Supreme Court writ powers:

1. A writ may run beyond the territory of a High Court when part of the cause of action arises within it.
2. For Fundamental Rights the aggrieved person must approach the High Court first before moving the Supreme Court.
3. A High Court may refuse a writ petition in its discretion, whereas the remedy of moving the Supreme Court under Article 32 for a Fundamental Right is itself guaranteed as a Fundamental Right.
4. The right to move the High Court under Article 226 is itself a Fundamental Right, like the Article 32 remedy.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 226(2). Statement 2 is incorrect: the two remedies are concurrent; either may be approached directly. Statement 3 is correct: A High Court has discretion to refuse a writ petition under Article 226, whereas the right to move the Supreme Court under Article 32 is itself a Fundamental Right in Part III. Statement 4 is incorrect: Article 32 is in Part III; Article 226 is not a Fundamental Right.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.164
'3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.164
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.164

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the refusal of a writ by a High Court:

1. Delay and laches by the petitioner are not a ground on which a High Court may refuse a writ.
2. Despite an alternative remedy it may entertain a petition where a Fundamental Right is violated, jurisdiction is lacking or natural justice is breached.
3. Disputed questions of fact and an alternative efficacious remedy are grounds on which it may refuse a writ.
4. Writ powers are used to control administrative excess and ensure the legality of quasi-judicial action.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: delay and laches and lack of bona fides are grounds for refusal. Statement 2 is correct: the recognised exceptions. Statement 3 is correct: Disputed questions of fact and an alternative efficacious remedy are grounds on which it may refuse a writ. Statement 4 is correct: Writ powers are used to control administrative excess and ensure the legality of quasi-judicial action.

concepts.name: Judicial activism, restraint and overreach, PIL, challenges and Lok Adalats
concepts.description: Judicial activism and review, restraint and overreach, Public Interest Litigation and its cases, challenges facing the judiciary, Lok Adalats and Permanent Lok Adalats.
concepts.idea: Courts have widened access through PIL and Lok Adalats while facing criticism of overreach and pendency.
concepts.rule: Judicial activism was coined in the USA and arrived in India in the mid-1970s; review is constitutional and negative, activism creative. PIL relaxes locus standi; leading cases are Hussainara Khatoon, Vishaka and Common Cause. Lok Adalats were created under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987; awards are deemed civil court decrees, final and binding with no appeal; non-compoundable offences are excluded. The Permanent Lok Adalat, added in 2002, handles public utility services, with a Chairman and two members, up to Rs 1 crore.
concepts.example: A letter from a prisoner is treated as a writ petition, and the dispute is settled in a Lok Adalat without appeal.

questions.q: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes judicial review from judicial activism?

questions.e: Judicial review has constitutional roots and is confined to legality and constitutionality; activism is proactive, creative and PIL-driven, often criticised as overreach.
w: It is the reverse: review is negative and corrective; activism is positive and creative.

Review is limited to legality; activism may extend into policy.

Audi alteram partem, under which both sides must be heard

concepts.name: Supreme Court and High Courts compared; the collegium and the judicial concepts
concepts.description: Side-by-side comparison of Supreme Court and High Courts and a revision of the collegium, judicial review, activism, restraint, overreach and Lok Adalats.
concepts.idea: Many rules for the Supreme Court have a parallel but different rule for High Courts.
concepts.rule: The Supreme Court is governed by Articles 124-147 and High Courts by Articles 214-231. Retirement is at 65 and 62, removal is the same, High Court judges can be transferred, Supreme Court judges cannot, and Article 226 is wider than Article 32. The collegium is judge-made through three cases. Judicial review is constitutional, activism proactive, restraint deferential and overreach encroaching; Lok Adalat awards cannot be appealed.
concepts.example: Transferring a High Court judge needs the CJI's consultation but a Supreme Court judge cannot be transferred.

questions.q: Which one of the following correctly matches the courts with the Articles of the Constitution that deal with them?
questions.a: The Supreme Court with Articles 124 to 147 and the High Courts with Articles 214 to 231
o: The Supreme Court with Articles 124 to 147 and the High Courts with Articles 214 to 231
The Supreme Court with Articles 214 to 231 and the High Courts with Articles 124 to 147
The Supreme Court with Articles 124 to 147 and the High Courts with Articles 233 to 237
The Supreme Court with Articles 52 to 78 and the High Courts with Articles 153 to 167
questions.e: Articles 124-147 in Part V govern the Supreme Court and Articles 214-231 in Part VI the High Courts (Laxmikanth ch26 p.414, ch34 p.508).
w: The two ranges are reversed.
Articles 233 to 237 deal with subordinate courts.
Those ranges deal with the Union and State executives.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements comparing Supreme Court and High Court judges is correct?
questions.a: A Supreme Court judge retires at 65 and a High Court judge at 62, and both are removed by the President on an address of Parliament
o: A Supreme Court judge retires at 65 and a High Court judge at 62, and both are removed by the President on an address of Parliament
Both retire at 65, but only the Supreme Court judge needs a parliamentary address for removal, a High Court judge being removed by the Governor
A Supreme Court judge retires at 62 and a High Court judge at 65, with the same removal procedure for both
A Supreme Court judge retires at 65 and a High Court judge at 62, and a High Court judge can be removed by the Governor
questions.e: Retirement is at 65 for the Supreme Court and 62 for High Courts; removal for proved misbehaviour or incapacity follows the same procedure.
w: High Court judges retire at 62 and are removed by the same procedure.
The ages are reversed.
Only the President removes High Court judges, on a parliamentary address.

questions.q: Which one of the following is correct about the transfer of judges?
questions.a: The President may transfer a High Court judge after consulting the CJI, but Supreme Court judges are not transferred
o: The President may transfer a High Court judge after consulting the CJI, but Supreme Court judges are not transferred
Both Supreme Court and High Court judges may be transferred from one court to another by the Chief Justice of India
A High Court judge may be transferred by the Governor of the State after consulting the State Chief Minister
A High Court judge can be transferred to another High Court only with his own consent, given in writing to the President
questions.e: Article 222 empowers the President; no equivalent provision exists for the Supreme Court. Transfer cannot be used as punishment (Laxmikanth ch34 p.510-511).
w: No transfer exists for Supreme Court judges and the President transfers High Court judges.
The Governor and Chief Minister have no role.
Consent is not required, though the transfer must be in public interest.

questions.q: The collegium system of appointing judges is
questions.a: not mentioned in the Constitution and was evolved by the Supreme Court through the Judges Cases
o: not mentioned in the Constitution and was evolved by the Supreme Court through the Judges Cases
provided in Article 124(2) as amended by the 99th Constitutional Amendment Act
introduced by Parliament in the Supreme Court Judges (Salaries and Conditions of Service) Act, 1958
provided in Article 217 for High Courts, Supreme Court judges being appointed by the President alone
questions.e: The collegium arose from the Second (1993) and Third (1998) Judges Cases; the 2015 verdict restored it.
w: The 99th Amendment tried to replace it with the NJAC and was struck down.
That Act deals with salaries and service conditions.
The collegium covers both courts and is judge-made.

questions.q: A court, finding that the legislature has not acted, frames detailed policy and takes over day-to-day administrative functions. This is best described as
questions.e: Overreach is a court acting beyond its jurisdiction in law-making, policy-making or administration, violating separation of powers.
w: Review examines the constitutionality of laws and actions.
Restraint is deference to the elected branches.
Advisory jurisdiction is the Supreme Court's opinion on a Presidential reference.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about comparing Supreme Court and High Court judges:

1. A Supreme Court judge retires at 65 and a High Court judge at 62.
2. The age of a High Court judge is decided by Parliament's chosen authority, and that of a Supreme Court judge by the President after consulting the CJI.
3. The oath is taken before the Chief Justice of India for Supreme Court judges and before the Chief Justice of the High Court for High Court judges.
4. Retired Supreme Court judges are barred from pleading before any court in India, whereas retired permanent High Court judges may plead before the Supreme Court and other High Courts.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Articles 124 and 217. Statement 2 is incorrect: it is the other way round. Statement 3 is incorrect: the oath is before the President or his nominee, and the Governor or his nominee, respectively. Statement 4 is correct: Laxmikanth ch26 p.418 and ch34 p.512.
w: '2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.418
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.418
'1 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.418

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about writ and original jurisdiction:

1. Article 32 is confined to Fundamental Rights, whereas Article 226 covers Fundamental Rights and other legal rights.
2. Both High Courts and the Supreme Court can be approached directly for Fundamental Rights.
3. Article 131 covers disputes between citizens and the Centre.
4. A High Court writ under Article 226 can reach a person outside its territory if the cause of action arises within it.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: 226 is wider. Statement 2 is correct: Concurrent. Statement 3 is incorrect: It covers Centre-State and inter-State disputes. Statement 4 is correct: Article 226(2).
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about removal and transfer:

1. Both Supreme Court and High Court judges are removed by the President after an address by each House of Parliament passed by special majority.
2. A High Court judge may be removed on grounds wider than for a Supreme Court judge, such as insolvency.
3. A High Court judge can be transferred after the President consults the CJI, while no transfer exists for Supreme Court judges.
4. A High Court judge's office falls vacant when he is elevated to the Supreme Court.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Same procedure. Statement 2 is incorrect: Proved misbehaviour or incapacity only. Statement 3 is correct: Article 222. Statement 4 is correct: To prevent two offices.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements comparing the jurisdictions of the Supreme Court and the High Courts:

1. Special leave to appeal against the judgment of any court or tribunal, except military ones, lies to the Supreme Court and not to the High Courts.
2. The appellate jurisdiction of a High Court is narrower than its first-instance jurisdiction.
3. Disputes about the election of members of Parliament and State legislatures are filed directly in the High Court, whereas Centre-State disputes go to the Supreme Court.
4. First appeals from district courts on law and fact lie directly to the Supreme Court.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 136. Statement 2 is incorrect: Laxmikanth ch34 p.514: the appellate jurisdiction is wider. Statement 3 is correct: original jurisdiction of each. Statement 4 is incorrect: first appeals lie to the High Court.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.514
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.514
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect: p.514

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about judicial concepts:

1. Judicial activism is constitutionally rooted in Articles 13, 32 and 226.
2. Judicial activism is not mentioned in the Constitution and evolved through judicial interpretation.
3. Judicial restraint is deference to other branches.
4. Judicial overreach is when a court encroaches on the executive or legislative domain.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: That describes judicial review. Statement 2 is correct: Typical. Statement 3 is correct: Defer. Statement 4 is correct: Criticised.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 1, which is incorrect

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about temporary judges:

1. The Supreme Court can have ad hoc judges for lack of quorum and High Courts can have additional judges for arrears.
2. The Supreme Court may appoint additional judges for a term up to two years.
3. Retired judges may be requested in both courts with the previous consent of the President and of the person.
4. An acting Chief Justice can be appointed in a High Court but not in the Supreme Court.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Articles 127 and 224. Statement 2 is incorrect: that is a High Court provision. Statement 3 is correct: Articles 128 and 224A. Statement 4 is incorrect: Articles 126 and 223 provide for it in both.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the finances of judges:

1. Supreme Court judges' salaries are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
2. High Court judges' salaries are charged on the State's Consolidated Fund.
3. The State's Consolidated Fund bears a High Court judge's pension.
4. According to Laxmikanth, retired judges of both courts get a pension of fifty per cent of the last drawn salary.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Non-votable. Statement 2 is correct: Laxmikanth ch34 p.512. Statement 3 is incorrect: On the Consolidated Fund of India. Statement 4 is correct: Per the chapter.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.512
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.512
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.512

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about appointment of judges:

1. A Supreme Court judge may be a distinguished jurist, whereas a High Court judge may not.
2. A Supreme Court judge needs ten years as a High Court judge, whereas a High Court judge needs five years of judicial office.
3. For High Court appointments the CJI, Governor and Chief Justice of the High Court are consulted.
4. For High Court appointments the collegium has the CJI and the four senior-most Supreme Court judges.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: only the Supreme Court has that route. Statement 2 is incorrect: the figures are swapped. Statement 3 is correct: for a judge other than the Chief Justice. Statement 4 is incorrect: it is the CJI and the two senior-most judges.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect
'3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about court powers:

1. The Supreme Court is a court of record under Article 129 and a High Court under Article 215.
2. The Supreme Court's review power is express under Article 137, whereas High Courts review as an inherent power.
3. A High Court cannot punish contempt of a subordinate court where the act is also an offence punishable under the Indian Penal Code (now the BNS).
4. Law declared by the Supreme Court binds all courts and that by a High Court binds subordinate courts in its territory.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Both. Statement 2 is correct: Different bases. Statement 3 is correct: Laxmikanth ch34 p.516 excludes such cases. Statement 4 is correct: Articles 141.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.516
'1, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.516
'1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.516

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Judges Cases and the collegium:

1. The First Judges Case held that consultation means concurrence.
2. The Second Judges Case gave birth to the collegium.
3. The Third Judges Case limited the collegium to three judges.
4. The Second Judges Case overruled the First.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: It held the opposite. Statement 2 is correct: 1993. Statement 3 is incorrect: It enlarged it. Statement 4 is correct: Reversal. So 2 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only one' is not the right count: exactly 2 of the statements are correct.
'Only three' is not the right count: exactly 2 of the statements are correct.
'All four' is not the right count: exactly 2 of the statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about jurisdiction:

1. Article 131 covers Centre-State and inter-State disputes.
2. Article 32 enforces any legal right of a citizen, not only Fundamental Rights.
3. Article 226 is limited to Fundamental Rights like Article 32.
4. Article 131 can be invoked by private individuals.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Yes. Statement 2 is incorrect: Article 32 is confined to Fundamental Rights. Statement 3 is incorrect: Wider. Statement 4 is incorrect: No. So 1 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'None' is not the right count: exactly 1 of the statements is correct.
'Only two' is not the right count: exactly 1 of the statements is correct.
'Only three' is not the right count: exactly 1 of the statements is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Lok Adalat awards:

1. A Lok Adalat award is final and binding with no right of appeal.
2. The award is deemed a decree of a civil court.
3. The Permanent Lok Adalat has a Chairman and two members.
4. Lok Adalats can try non-compoundable offences.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Frequently tested. Statement 2 is correct: Yes. Statement 3 is correct: Yes. Statement 4 is incorrect: Excluded. So 3 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'None' is not the right count: exactly 3 of the statements are correct.
'Only two' is not the right count: exactly 3 of the statements are correct.
'All four' is not the right count: exactly 3 of the statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The collegium system finds no mention in the text of the Constitution.
Statement-II: The collegium was evolved by the Supreme Court in the Second (1993) and Third (1998) Judges Cases.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct

Rejected: Statement-I is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: A Lok Adalat award cannot be appealed.
Statement-II: An aggrieved party can approach the District Court against the award.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct. Statement-II is incorrect. No appeal lies to any court.
w: Rejected: Statement-II is incorrect.
Rejected: Statement-II is incorrect.
Rejected: Statement-I is correct.
